`/work/fatex_004.lean` now compiles with no errors and no `sorry` warning. The only output is linter warnings: a deprecated `Set.mem_setOf_eq` and two unused `Finset.mem_coe` simp arguments. I changed only the proof body and kept the imports, namespace and theorem statement as they were.

The proof follows this argument:

1. **Count the Sylow `p`-subgroups.** The number of Sylow `p`-subgroups is congruent to 1 mod `p` and divides `p + 1`. It is not 1, because a single Sylow subgroup would be normal. So there are exactly `p + 1` of them, each of order `p` and equal to its own normalizer.
2. **Count the elements of order `p`.** Distinct Sylow `p`-subgroups share only the identity, so there are at least `(p + 1)(p − 1)` elements of order `p`.
3. **Large conjugacy classes.** Take any prime `q` dividing `p + 1` and an element `x` of order `q`. If `p` divided the order of the centralizer of `x`, then `x` would commute with some element `z` of order `p`. That would put `x` in the normalizer of `⟨z⟩`, which is `⟨z⟩` itself, so `q` would divide `p`, a contradiction. So the centralizer has order dividing `p + 1`, and the conjugacy class of `x` has at least `p` elements, all of order `q`.
4. **Only the prime 2 can divide `p + 1`.** Suppose an odd prime `q` divides `p + 1`. Take a class of order-2 elements and a class of order-`q` elements, each with at least `p` elements. Together with the identity and the order-`p` elements, these give more than `p(p + 1)` elements, which is impossible. Hence 2 is the only prime dividing `p + 1`, so `p + 1` is a power of 2.
